name: Blue City Walking Tour
description: Walk through the warren of blue-painted houses in the old city at the foot of Mehrangarh Fort.

name: Clock Tower & Sardar Market
description: Iconic clock tower in the heart of the old city. Bustling market selling spices, textiles, and handicrafts.

name: Jaswant Thada
description: Intricately carved white marble cenotaph built in 1899. Called "Taj Mahal of Marwar" with beautiful lake views.

name: Mandore Gardens
description: Former Rathore capital with royal cenotaphs in red sandstone. Hall of Heroes with carved figures of deities.

name: Mehrangarh Fort
description: One of India's largest forts, towering 400 ft above the Blue City. Magnificent museum, courtyards, and zip-lining.

name: Rao Jodha Desert Rock Park
description: Ecologically restored desert park below Mehrangarh Fort. 70+ acres with 300+ species of desert plants.

name: Toorji Ka Jhalra Stepwell
description: Beautifully restored 18th-century stepwell in the old city. Geometric water architecture.

name: Umaid Bhawan Palace
description: Art Deco masterpiece and world's largest private residence. Part museum, part Taj hotel, part royal residence.

name: Gobindgarh Fort
description: Restored 18th-century fort with 7D theatre, live shows, and Sikh heritage galleries. Night experience excellent.

name: Golden Temple
description: Holiest shrine in Sikhism. Free langar feeds 100,000+ daily.

name: Hall Bazaar
description: Bustling market street leading to the Golden Temple. Phulkari dupattas, juttis, and street food.

name: Jallianwala Bagh
description: Memorial at the site of the 1919 British massacre. Bullet marks visible.

name: Partition Museum
description: India's first museum dedicated to the 1947 Partition. Personal stories, artifacts, and multimedia displays.

name: Wagah Border Ceremony
description: Daily flag-lowering ceremony at the India-Pakistan border.

name: Gwalior Fort
description: One of India's most impregnable forts. Man Singh Palace with blue tilework, Sas Bahu temples, Teli Ka Mandir.

name: Jai Vilas Palace & Museum
description: Opulent palace with world's largest pair of chandeliers (3.5 tons each) and a silver toy train serving dinner.

name: Man Singh Palace
description: Masterpiece inside Gwalior Fort with vibrant blue and yellow tilework. Architectural marvel of the 15th century.

name: Sun Temple (Saas Bahu Temple)
description: Twin 11th-century temples inside Gwalior Fort with intricate carvings. Wrongly called Saas Bahu (mother-in-law, daughter-in-law).

name: Tomb of Tansen
description: Memorial of the legendary Mughal court musician. People chew leaves of the tamarind tree here believing it improves voice.

name: Griddhakuta (Vulture Peak)
description: Hill where Buddha delivered many sermons including the Lotus Sutra. Sacred Buddhist pilgrimage site.

name: Rajgir Hot Springs (Brahmakund)
description: Ancient hot springs mentioned in Buddhist and Jain texts. Temperature 45°C. Separate bathing areas.

name: Venuvana Vihar (Bamboo Grove)
description: First Buddhist monastery — bamboo grove gifted to Buddha by King Bimbisara. Sacred pilgrimage garden.

name: Vishwa Shanti Stupa (Rajgir)
description: Peace pagoda atop Ratnagiri Hill reached by aerial chairlift. Panoramic views of Rajgir valley.

name: Devalia Safari Park
description: Fenced interpretation zone with guaranteed lion sightings. 45-min bus safari. Perfect for families wanting certainty.

name: Gir Lion Safari
description: Jeep safari through dry deciduous forest. 700+ Asiatic lions, leopards, crocodiles, and 300+ bird species.

name: Kamleshwar Dam
description: Dam inside the park with resident marsh crocodiles. Bird watching hub — painted storks, flamingos, eagles.

name: Mandvi Shipbuilding Yard
description: Traditional wooden dhow-building yard still operational. Craftsmen build ships by hand using centuries-old techniques.

name: Vijay Vilas Palace
description: 400-year-old palace with private beach. Used in Bollywood's Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam. Ornate Rajput architecture.

name: Wind Farm Beach
description: Pristine beach with windmills dotting the coastline. Less crowded than the main beach. Golden sunsets.

name: GHNP Tirthan Entrance
description: Main gateway to UNESCO Great Himalayan National Park. Permits and guides available.

name: Serolsar Lake
description: Sacred high-altitude lake reached via trek from Jalori Pass. Budhi Nagin temple on its banks.

name: Tirthan River Trout Fishing
description: Catch-and-release trout fishing in crystal-clear waters. Guided fishing trips available.

name: Bomdila Monastery (Lower Gompa)
description: Tibetan Buddhist monastery with views of the Arunachal ranges. Replica of Tsona Gontse in Tibet.

name: Bomdila View Point
description: Panoramic views of the eastern Himalayan range and Tawang road. Clear sunrise views of snow peaks.

name: Kanha Museum & Interpretation Centre
description: Interactive displays about the park's ecosystem, tiger conservation, and the barasingha rescue story.

name: Kanha Tiger Safari
description: Inspiration for Kipling's "The Jungle Book". Vast sal and bamboo forests. Best for barasingha (swamp deer).

name: Gauri Kund
description: A smaller sacred pool ~1km before the main Manimahesh Lake, where women pilgrims traditionally bathe before darshan.

name: Manimahesh Lake (Dal Lake)
description: The glacial lake at 3,950m below Manimahesh Kailash peak, the destination of the annual Manimahesh Yatra. Pilgrims circumambulate the lake before darshan.

name: Kapileshwar Mahadev Cave Temple
description: Cave temple 3 km from town with geological rock formations and Shiva shrine inside.

name: Pithoragarh Fort (London Fort)
description: Gorkha-era fort at the edge of town with views of snow-capped Panchachuli peaks.

name: Barak Waterfall
description: Towering 230-ft waterfall in the Tamenglong district. Accessible via a moderate forest trek.

name: Zeilad Lake
description: Sacred natural lake surrounded by hills. Important cultural site for the Zeliangrong Naga people.

name: Baleshwar Temple Complex
description: Cluster of beautifully carved stone temples from the Chand dynasty era with intricate Nagara architecture.

name: Gopinath Temple
description: Ancient Shiva temple with a trident embedded in stone that no one has been able to remove. Legends abound.

name: Neermahal Water Palace
description: India's largest water palace in the middle of Rudrasagar Lake. Mughal and Hindu architecture blend.

name: Tungnath Temple
description: World's highest Shiva temple (Panch Kedar) at 12,073 ft. Over 1,000 years old with stunning architecture.
